source: Waltz, Lau, Grewal, Holyoak (2000) The role of working memory in analogical mapping
finding: A digit-string memory load cut relational mappings in cross-mapped picture pairs. Asking for three mappings at once raised relational mappings.
numbers: Exp 1, N=45 UCLA students, 2x2 between-subjects (1-map vs 3-map instruction; 7-digit load vs none). Relational proportion: 3-map .60 vs 1-map .39, F(1,41)=6.64, p<.05. Load .35 vs no load .64, F(1,41)=12.48, p<.01. No interaction, F<1.
limits: Pictures were the 8 Markman & Gentner (1993) pairs. Between-subjects, small cells. Verbal load only.
agent_relevance: Direct human evidence that relational mapping needs working memory. Asking for several mappings at once may push a model toward relational answers.

source: Waltz, Lau, Grewal, Holyoak (2000) The role of working memory in analogical mapping
finding: The digit load was near capacity, and failures were not random. Most non-relational answers were attribute matches.
numbers: Full digit-string recall about .50 (the classic span limit), no difference by number of objects mapped (M=.50 single vs .38 multiple, t(21)=1.11, p>.20). 7.5% of all mappings were neither relational nor attribute.
limits: The secondary task was scored for recall, not tied to mapping quality trial by trial.
agent_relevance: Under load, reasoners fall back to surface matching. Watch for the same failure in an LLM with a crowded context.

source: Waltz, Lau, Grewal, Holyoak (2000) The role of working memory in analogical mapping
finding: Experiment 2 replicated the load effect with two different loads, a phonological one and an executive one.
numbers: N=109, 2x3 between-subjects (1-map vs 3-map; no load, repeat the word 'the', random-digit generation). Relational proportion: 3-map .37 vs 1-map .25, F(1,103)=9.61, p<.01. No load .45 vs both loads .24, F(1,103)=23.70, p<.01. Distractor main effect F(2,103)=11.87, p<.01.
limits: Overall relational rates are low (.25 to .45) because the pictures are cross-mapped by design.
agent_relevance: Both buffer-like and executive-like loads harm structure mapping.

source: Waltz, Lau, Grewal, Holyoak (2000) The role of working memory in analogical mapping
finding: The phonological and executive loads hurt equally, so the data cannot separate the two working-memory parts.
numbers: Phonological M=.23 vs random-digit generation M=.25, F(1,103)<1. No interaction of load with mapping instruction, F(2,103)<1. Only 5% of mappings were neither relational nor attribute.
limits: Null result between load types. Authors read it as mapping needing both modality-specific and executive resources.
agent_relevance: No clean split of storage limits versus control limits in mapping. Treat the limit as one pool.

source: Waltz, Lau, Grewal, Holyoak (2000) The role of working memory in analogical mapping
finding: The authors tie the result to capacity-limited mapping models: Halford's relational complexity and Hummel and Holyoak's LISA.
numbers: Text only. Prediction: any manipulation that reduces working-memory capacity should make relational mappings harder and attribute mappings more common.
limits: General prediction, not a test of one model against another.
agent_relevance: Gives the formal prediction to borrow: cut available slots and expect a shift from relations to attributes.

source: Tohill & Holyoak (2000) The impact of anxiety on analogical reasoning
finding: Induced state anxiety cut relational mapping. Errors shifted to attribute mappings.
numbers: Exp 1, N=22, serial-subtraction anxiety induction. STAI state means 43.0 vs 32.7, F(1,20)=8.90, p=.008. Relational mappings 45% vs 68%, F(1,20)=5.78, p=.026. Attribute 51% vs 24%. About 8% neither.
limits: Very small N. Anxiety might change preference rather than capacity (Exp 2 tests this).
agent_relevance: Anything that drains capacity (worry, noise, side tasks) hurts mapping. Keep prompts calm and uncluttered.

source: Tohill & Holyoak (2000) The impact of anxiety on analogical reasoning
finding: The effect survived instructions to choose the relational match, so it was not only a preference shift.
numbers: Exp 2, N=22. STAI 42.6 vs 33.4, F(1,20)=5.71, p=.03. Relational mappings 72% vs 84%, F(1,20)=5.09, p=.04. Gap 12 points versus 23 points in Exp 1.
limits: Instruction shrinks but does not remove the gap. Small N.
agent_relevance: Telling the model which relation to match narrows the gap but does not close it.

source: Tohill & Holyoak (2000) The impact of anxiety on analogical reasoning
finding: Theory link: Eysenck's working-memory restriction theory says anxiety takes executive resources, so complex relational mapping should drop first.
numbers: Theory section. Anxiety is held to act on the executive controller and leave simple processing relatively unaffected.
limits: Processing-efficiency theory says extra effort can compensate. Data are correlational with the theory.
agent_relevance: Capacity is one shared pool that other demands can drain.

source: Cowan (2010) The magical mystery four: how is working memory capacity limited, and why?
finding: Core working-memory capacity is about 3 to 5 chunks in young adults, not Miller's 7. The limit shows when rehearsal and chunking are blocked.
numbers: Abstract: central store limited to 3 to 5 meaningful items. Longer verbal chunks such as idioms: 3 or 4 recalled (Gilchrist, Cowan, Naveh-Benjamin 2008). Search is most efficient with groups of about 3.5 items.
quote: a central memory store limited to 3 to 5 meaningful items in young adults
limits: Slot versus resource accounts remain debated, and so does what counts as a chunk.
agent_relevance: A number to carry into design. Map in sets of about 3 to 4 correspondences at a time.

source: Gong, Wan, Wang (2023) Working memory capacity of ChatGPT: an empirical study
finding: ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) shows a working-memory limit on the n-back task. Sensitivity drops sharply from n=1 to n=3, like humans.
numbers: Verbal n-back, n=1 to 3, 50 blocks per setting (30 in the model comparison). In the base, feedback and CoT variants d fell to about 1 at n=3. Adding noise lowered capacity further.
limits: One main model. 'Human-like' is the authors' reading. n-back is not a mapping task.
agent_relevance: First measured span-like limit in an LLM. A rough bound on how many items to track serially without notes.

source: Gong, Wan, Wang (2023) Working memory capacity of ChatGPT: an empirical study
finding: Spatial n-back showed the same decline. Chain-of-thought helped. Larger grids raised capacity, which has no human test.
numbers: Four spatial variants matched the verbal ones. CoT 'significantly improved' performance. Grids 3x3, 4x4, 5x5, 7x7. Abstract-reasoning spatial variants had lower capacity than the base.
limits: No human spatial-grid comparison was run.
agent_relevance: Writing steps down raises the effective limit. Supports an external mapping table at O7.

source: Gong, Wan, Wang (2023) Working memory capacity of ChatGPT: an empirical study
finding: GPT-4 far exceeds the other models. Seven open models (Bloomz, ChatGLM, Vicuna) had very low capacity and looked alike.
numbers: Models: Bloomz-7B1 and mt, ChatGLM-6B v1.0 and v1.1, Vicuna-7B and 13B, GPT-4, plus 3.5. GPT-4 was not tested above n=3 because of cost, so its true limit is unknown.
limits: Cost hid GPT-4's ceiling.
agent_relevance: Capacity differs by model. Measure our own base model before fixing a batch size.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: GPT-3 matched or beat UCLA undergraduates on zero-shot digit-matrix problems.
numbers: Humans N=40. Generative: OR=1.88, p=0.005, CI [1.21, 2.91]. Multiple choice: OR=6.27, p=2.3e-8, CI [3.28, 11.99]. The best human got every problem right. Subtype profile correlation r(30)=0.39, p=0.027.
limits: Possible training-data overlap. Authors note some participants beat GPT-3.
agent_relevance: LLMs can do relational mapping at moderate load without an obvious human-style bottleneck.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: On letter-string analogies GPT-3 beat humans overall, mostly on problems needing no generalisation. Both fall as generalisations rise.
numbers: Overall OR=1.76, p=6.3e-5, CI [1.34, 2.31]. Zero-generalisation: OR=1.76, p=0.0007. Number of generalisations, GPT-3: OR=0.51, p=2e-16. Story analogies: humans better, OR=0.37, p=0.0003.
limits: Later work (Hodel and West; Lewis and Mitchell) found fragility. Small human samples per condition.
agent_relevance: Falling accuracy with more relations to carry looks load-like. More relations at once, worse mapping.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: The authors say it is unclear how GPT-3 maps. They name the human account (systematic comparison of explicit relational representations) and ask whether GPT-3 has emergent relational representations.
numbers: Discussion text. Cites Halford, Wilson and Phillips on relational complexity.
limits: No mechanism test.
agent_relevance: A capacity-limited serial mapper is a human mechanism. Whether an LLM uses one is open.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2024) Evidence from counterfactual tasks supports emergent analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Reply to Hodel and West and Lewis and Mitchell. With a shuffled alphabet, GPT-4 with code execution matched humans.
numbers: Humans N=99 (interval 1) and 97 (interval 2). Human vs GPT-4: P=8.9e-13. Human vs GPT-4+code: P=0.496. Interval 2 harder for humans (P=1.5e-11) and GPT-4 (P<2e-16), not significant for GPT-4+code (P=0.066).
limits: Code execution is not a humanlike route. The authors say so.
agent_relevance: Offloading position bookkeeping to code removed the failure. Same idea as a code-held mapping table.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2024) Evidence from counterfactual tasks supports emergent analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: GPT-4 errors resemble human errors: many used a valid alternative rule.
numbers: 46% (23/50) of GPT-4's errors were valid alternative rules, versus 39% of human errors in the Lewis and Mitchell data.
limits: Small error sample (50).
agent_relevance: Do not score mapping by one answer key. Score by structure.

source: Lewis & Mitchell (2024) Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate the generality of analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: GPT-3, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 drop on counterfactual letter-string analogies (permuted alphabets, then symbols). Humans stay roughly flat.
numbers: Human accuracy stayed near constant across 0, 2, 5, 10 and 20 permuted letters. GPT models fell step by step and fell again for symbol sequences. Their humans scored higher than in Webb et al. GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 were no better than GPT-3.
limits: Prompt wording matters. Webb et al. 2024 reply that code execution closes the gap.
agent_relevance: Success on familiar forms may be recall, not mapping. Test on novel relations.

source: Lewis & Mitchell (2024) Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate the generality of analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Error types differ. LLMs make more 'incorrect rule' errors than humans, and humans find more alternative rules.
numbers: Share of sampled errors, alternative rule: GPT-3 5.81%, GPT-4 22.00%, humans 38.59%. Incorrect rule: GPT-3 30.97%, GPT-4 32.67%, humans 14.67%.
limits: Hand-coded samples, about 160 per model and 184 for humans.
agent_relevance: LLMs are less inventive mappers than people. Do not assume human-like mapping.

source: Hodel & West (2023) Response: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: GPT-3 fails simple variants of the letter-string problems, so the zero-shot claim is not general. They also point to training-data overlap.
numbers: Their synthetic-alphabet test gives GPT-3 at least 30% of its original accuracy (text wording). Quoting the Webb authors: GPT-3 may have seen letter-string problems on web pages.
limits: Short comment paper, GPT-3 only. GPT-4 was answered by Webb et al. 2024.
agent_relevance: Treat any LLM analogy success as suspect until novel structure is tested.

source: Musker, Duchnowski, Milliere, Pavlick (2025) LLMs as models for analogical reasoning
finding: New tasks map semantic content to abstract symbols. Advanced LLMs (GPT-4, Claude 3, Llama-405B) matched human accuracy in several conditions.
numbers: Conditions: Defaults, Permuted Pairs, Distracted, Only RHS, Numeric Dual-attribute. The Distracted condition lowered performance by about 0.25 for all four subject types.
limits: Mostly university student participants. Models respond differently to some variations.
agent_relevance: Distractors cost both humans and models. Prune irrelevant correspondences before mapping.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners
finding: Asking the model to write its own relevant examples first beat 0-shot CoT and manual few-shot CoT on GSM8K, MATH, Codeforces and BIG-Bench.
numbers: Qualitative claim from the abstract. Table rows were garbled on extraction, so no row values are recorded.
limits: This is analogical retrieval of examples, not capacity-limited mapping. No working-memory test.
agent_relevance: Do not cite as evidence for serial mapping. Useful only as a sibling for retrieval.

source: Keane & Brayshaw (1988) The Incremental Analogy Machine (IAM)
finding: IAM builds a mapping in steps instead of one parallel match, so it has a working-memory-like limit. From memory: it seeds a small set of matches and extends them, and input order changes the result.
numbers: Not opened. No numbers recorded.
limits: Primary paper not read. Only listed in our SUBFIELDS file. Verify before use.
agent_relevance: Candidate rule: map a few correspondences, then extend, rather than all at once.

source: Keane, Ledgeway, Duff (1994) Constraints on analogical mapping: a comparison of three models
finding: From memory: compared SME, ACME and IAM against human mapping data. Serial IAM predicted human mapping effects such as order effects.
numbers: Not opened. No numbers recorded.
limits: Not read this session.
agent_relevance: A test set that separates serial from parallel mappers.

source: Halford, Wilson, Phillips (1998) Processing capacity defined by relational complexity
finding: From memory: adults process about four related variables at once. Relational complexity (the number of related arguments) sets the limit.
numbers: Not opened. No numbers recorded.
limits: Not read; cited by Waltz et al. and Webb et al.
agent_relevance: A way to count how many relations a mapping step holds at once.

source: Hummel & Holyoak (1997) Distributed representations of structure (LISA)
finding: From memory: LISA maps by timed firing of role-filler bindings in a small working memory. Limits come from how many bindings can fire out of phase.
numbers: Not opened. No numbers recorded.
limits: Not read; Waltz et al. cite it for the capacity prediction.
agent_relevance: A formal model linking limited slots to mapping errors.

source: Hummel & Holyoak (2003) A symbolic-connectionist theory of relational inference and generalization
finding: From memory: extends LISA to inference and schema induction. Relational generalisation stays capacity limited.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: The candidate-inference step is capacity limited too.

source: Cowan (2001) The magical number 4 in short-term memory
finding: From memory: capacity of about 4 chunks when rehearsal and grouping are blocked.
numbers: Not opened. Cowan 2010 (opened) states the 3 to 5 range.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Same as the Cowan 2010 line.

source: Markman & Gentner (1993) Structural alignment during similarity comparisons
finding: From memory and Waltz et al.: asking people to map three objects at once pushes them to relational matches in cross-mapped pictures.
numbers: Not opened. Replication numbers are in the Waltz lines.
limits: Only the replication was read.
agent_relevance: Supports 'map several at once' as a way to force structure.

source: Waltz et al. (1999) A system for relational reasoning in human prefrontal cortex
finding: From memory: patients with prefrontal damage did worse than controls once problems needed integrating two relations rather than one.
numbers: Not opened. Details from memory only.
limits: Not read. Verify before use.
agent_relevance: Neural parallel to the capacity limit on relational integration.
